meta.notDerived: No data has been derived yet.

filters.title: Report filters
filters.wipByColumnHint: Board columns need one team: pick a team (not All teams or Unassigned) and clear the domain.

velocity.title: Velocity
velocity.description: How much each team planned into a sprint: the scope committed at the start (initial) against the scope it ended with (final).
velocity.chartTitle: Initial and final scope per sprint
velocity.chartLabel: Chart: initial and final scope by sprint
velocity.snapshot: Frozen at completion: initial {{initialMd}} MD, final {{finalMd}} MD

throughput.title: Throughput
throughput.description: What each team delivered: the work finished per week or month, and the scope done inside each sprint. The two views differ by design — a task finished after its sprint closed counts in the period only.

caption.TASK: Domain view: delivered in — a task counts in its own domain.
caption.EPIC: Domain view: earned in — a task counts in its epic's domain.

throughput.sprintCaption: The sprint view: what was done inside each sprint while it was in it, priced at the sprint's close. It ignores the domain, activity type and work category filters.
throughput.bucketTableLabel: Delivered per period, as a table

sprintConsistency.title: Sprint consistency
sprintConsistency.description: How a sprint's scope moved: what was committed, what was added and removed on the way, and where the final scope ended up.
sprintConsistency.scopeLabel: Chart: committed and delivered scope by sprint
sprintConsistency.partitionTitle: Where the final scope ended up
sprintConsistency.partitionCaption: Final scope = delivered + carried over + dropped, so each bar's height is the sprint's final scope.
sprintConsistency.partitionLabel: Chart: final scope split into carried over, delivered and dropped, by sprint
sprintConsistency.changesLabel: Chart: scope added and removed during each sprint
sprintConsistency.tableCaption: Man-days, with the item count in brackets.
sprintConsistency.snapshot: Frozen at completion: committed {{committed}} · final {{final}} · delivered {{delivered}} MD

minSample.distribution_one: Only {{count}} item in this selection — at least {{min}} are needed to show percentiles and a histogram.
minSample.distribution_other: Only {{count}} items in this selection — at least {{min}} are needed to show percentiles and a histogram.
minSample.share_one: Only {{count}} item started in this selection — at least {{min}} are needed to show a share.
minSample.share_other: Only {{count}} items started in this selection — at least {{min}} are needed to show a share.
minSample.none: Nothing to measure in this selection.
minSample.thresholds_one: Only {{count}} finished item in the window — at least {{min}} are needed to show thresholds, so no item is banded.
minSample.thresholds_other: Only {{count}} finished items in the window — at least {{min}} are needed to show thresholds, so no item is banded.
minSample.thresholdsNone: No finished item in the window yet, so there are no thresholds and no item is banded.

distribution.histogramLabel: Histogram: number of items per range

ratio.hint: A ratio of 1 means the actual cost equals the estimate; above 1 it cost more.

groupsCaption.distribution: Groups below the minimum sample show counts only.

taskAccuracy.title: Task estimation accuracy
taskAccuracy.description: How the actual cost of finished tasks compares with their estimate: actual man-days ÷ estimate. The estimate at start is the primary view; the estimate at done is the second.
taskAccuracy.startCaption: Primary view — the estimate the team committed to when work began.
taskAccuracy.doneCaption: Second view — the estimate as it stood when the task finished.

excluded.neverStarted: Never started, so no estimate at start
excluded.unestimatedAtStart: No estimate at start (including estimated late)

epicAccuracy.title: Epic estimation accuracy
epicAccuracy.description: How the actual cost of finished epics compares with their OWN estimate: actual man-days ÷ own estimate. The sum of the child estimates is shown beside it, never used as the estimate.
epicAccuracy.startTitle: Against the own estimate at start
epicAccuracy.doneTitle: Against the own estimate at done

excluded.noActual: No time logged on the epic or its children
excluded.neverStarted: Never started, so no estimate at start
excluded.unestimatedAtStart: No own estimate at start (the child sum is never used)

epicAccuracy.epicsTruncated: Showing the newest {{count}} epics; the distributions above count all of them.

adjustments.title: Estimate adjustments
adjustments.description: How often an estimate changes after work has started, and by how much between start and done. An estimate that only appeared after start is counted separately, never as an infinite change.
adjustments.changeHint: (estimate at done − estimate at start) ÷ estimate at start; +25% means the estimate grew by a quarter.

excluded.estimatedLate: Estimated late — no estimate at start
excluded.unestimated: No estimate at start or at done (or never started)

adjustments.lateNote: Estimated late is included in Changed after start.
adjustments.domainViewNote: The domain view applies to tasks; epics always read their own space.

epicsNotPerPerson: Epics aren't attributed to individual people, so there are no epic figures for a single person.

cycleTime.title: Cycle time
cycleTime.description: How long finished tasks took from first start to done — in working days (the primary view, on the configured calendar) and in elapsed calendar days. A reopened task counts its whole span. Finished epics follow in their own card, by owner team.
cycleTime.workingCaption: Primary view — days on the configured working calendar.
cycleTime.elapsedCaption: Second view — wall-clock days, weekends and holidays included.

excluded.neverStarted: Never started (created straight into done), so no cycle

cycleTime.trendTitle: Trend: median and p90 per period
cycleTime.trendCaption: Working days, by the period each task finished in. A period with too few items has no line point — a gap, never a zero.
cycleTime.trendAllHidden: No period has enough finished items to show a median and p90.
cycleTime.trendLabel: Chart: median and p90 cycle time in working days by period

epics.title: Epics
epics.caption: Epics finished in the period, by the team that owns their domain. An epic's cycle runs from its own first start to its own done, and it is never attributed to a person.
epics.neverStarted: Epics never started (finished without a start), so no cycle
epics.none: No epics finished in this period.

reportedTime.title: Reported time
reportedTime.description: How much of the elapsed working time was logged: man-days logged ÷ working days of cycle time. It is not flow efficiency, which is the share of the cycle spent actively in progress (shown beside it).
reportedTime.ratioCaption: Man-days logged per working day of cycle time — 1 means a full day logged for every working day.
reportedTime.outlierNote: Very short cycles give very large ratios. They are real and never dropped, so read the median (p50) first — the mean, p95 and the top of the histogram can be dominated by them.
reportedTime.flowCaption: Active time ÷ cycle time: time in progress and not blocked, as a share of the whole cycle. Logged time plays no part.

wip.title: WIP
wip.description: How many items sit in each stage, status or board column at the end of every day. The bands are stacked, so the top edge is their total.
wip.chartTitle: Items at the end of each day

caption.STAGE: By stage. Not started and Done are hidden at first: Not started holds the whole backlog and Done only ever grows. Tick them to see all the work.
caption.STATUS: By status, ordered by stage and then by name.
caption.COLUMN: By column of the team's board, in board order.

wip.bothNote: Tasks and epics are different grains; counting both adds them together.
wip.chartLabel: Chart: items at the end of each day, stacked by band
wip.noneShown: Tick at least one band to draw the chart.
wip.summaryLabel: Latest day, average and peak per band, as a table
wip.columnNeedsBoard: This team has no board mapped, so its items cannot be counted by board column. Count by stage or status instead, or map a board in the data source configuration.
wip.summaryNote: These figures cover every calendar day of the period, whatever the chart shows.

backlog.title: Estimated backlog
backlog.description: Estimated work that has not started: level-0 tasks with their own estimate that sit in no started sprint, counted at the end of each day. A parent estimated only through its sub-tasks is not in it (a known gap).
backlog.noVelocity: No closed sprint yet, or this selection has no velocity of its own (the unowned backlog or a domain slice), so it cannot be expressed in sprints.
backlog.zeroVelocity: The recent sprints delivered nothing, so the backlog cannot be expressed in sprints.
backlog.basisShort: Fewer closed sprints than the window, so the pace is less certain.
backlog.unitNote: At unit level the pace is the sum of each team's own mean, set against the whole backlog, including the part no team owns, so a large unowned backlog inflates the figure.
backlog.chartCaption: Man-days at the end of each day; the tooltip and the table add the item count.
backlog.chartLabel: Chart: estimated backlog in man-days by day
backlog.tableLabel: Backlog by day, as a table
backlog.basis_one: Recent pace: {{md}} MD delivered per sprint, the mean of {{count}} closed sprint (window: {{window}}).
backlog.basis_other: Recent pace: {{md}} MD delivered per sprint, the mean of {{count}} closed sprints (window: {{window}}).
backlog.unitBasis_one: Recent pace: the sum of each team's own mean delivery per sprint, {{md}} MD, from at least {{count}} closed sprint per team (window: {{window}}).
backlog.unitBasis_other: Recent pace: the sum of each team's own mean delivery per sprint, {{md}} MD, from at least {{count}} closed sprints per team (window: {{window}}).
backlog.unitBasisShort: Some team has fewer closed sprints than the window, so the pace is less certain.

agingWip.title: Aging WIP
agingWip.description: The work in progress right now and how long each item has been going: working days from its first start until now. Age is as of now, so the period does not apply; the bands compare each age with the team's recent finished items.
agingWip.caption: Age is counted on the configured working calendar. Blocked is as of the last derive.
agingWip.thresholdsCaption: Cycle time, in working days, of the team's last finished items. An item is banded by the highest threshold its age is above.
agingWip.basis_one: Based on the last {{count}} finished item.
agingWip.basis_other: Based on the last {{count}} finished items.
agingWip.unitNote: At unit level the window spans the whole unit — pick a team for its own thresholds.
agingWip.userNote: Thresholds belong to the team: a member's items are read against the team's window.
agingWip.empty: Nothing is in progress right now.
agingWip.truncated: Showing the oldest {{count}} items; more match. Narrow the team or the domain to see the rest.

blockedTime.title: Blocked time
blockedTime.description: How long finished items spent blocked — flagged or in a blocked status — in working days and as a share of their cycle. An item that was never blocked is a real zero and stays in the first distribution.
blockedTime.daysCaption: Every finished item in the period; an item never blocked counts as zero.
blockedTime.shareCaption: Blocked working days ÷ cycle working days, for the items that have a cycle.
blockedTime.topCaption: Up to 20 finished items with the most blocked working days, newest first among equals.
blockedTime.topEmpty: No finished item was blocked in this period.
blockedTime.topTableLabel: Most blocked items, as a table
blockedTime.groupsTasksOnly: The groups cover tasks only (epics have no assignee), so they add up to the tasks' total, not to the totals above.
blockedTime.blockedItems_one: {{count}} of {{total}} finished items was blocked at all; the rest are zeros and stay in the distribution.
blockedTime.blockedItems_other: {{count}} of {{total}} finished items were blocked at all; the rest are zeros and stay in the distribution.

epicProgress.title: Epic progress
epicProgress.description: Planned value (PV), earned value (EV) and actual cost (AC) in man-days, added up from the beginning of time to the as-of day, with the schedule variance SV = EV − PV, the cost variance CV = EV − AC, the schedule performance index SPI = EV ÷ PV and the cost performance index CPI = EV ÷ AC. The period only chooses which days the curves show; the figures always include everything before it.

levelNote.UNIT: Epic-attributed work only: a task with no epic has no plan to compare against. The domains below add up to these figures; the teams do not.
levelNote.DOMAIN: Epic-attributed work only: a task with no epic has no plan to compare against.
levelNote.EPIC: The plan is the epic's current baseline spread evenly over the working days between its start and due dates.
levelNote.TEAM: Sprint view: planned is the committed scope of the team's sprints on the day each starts, earned is what those sprints delivered, and cost is the time the team's members logged. It does not add up to the unit's figures.

epicProgress.spiNone: No plan yet: planned value is 0, so there is no ratio.
epicProgress.cpiNone: Nothing logged yet: actual cost is 0, so there is no ratio.
epicProgress.foreignHint: Share of the time this team's members logged (up to the as-of day) that went into other teams' work. Read the team's CPI together with it.
epicProgress.foreignNone: Nothing logged yet, so there is no share.

breadcrumb.label: Where you are in the drill-down

epicProgress.chartCaption: Man-days at the end of each day, added up from the beginning of time.
epicProgress.chartLabel: Chart: cumulative planned value, earned value and actual cost in man-days by day
epicProgress.tableLabel: Cumulative PV, EV and AC by day, as a table
epicProgress.domainsCaption: Epic basis: these rows add up to the unit's figures above.
epicProgress.teamsCaption: Sprint basis: planned is each team's committed sprint scope, earned what those sprints delivered, cost the time its members logged. A different view from the domains: these rows do not add up to the unit's figures.
epicProgress.epicsCaption: Epics of this domain that have a plan or any earned value or cost; the domain's totals above stay authoritative.
epicProgress.noRows: Nothing to list as of this day.

epic.title: Plan
epic.budgetChildren: the sum of its tasks' estimates
epic.driftDates: Dates moved since the original plan
epic.driftBudget: Budget changed since the original plan
epic.noHorizon: No plan curve: the plan is missing a date, or a date lies more than ten years from today, so planned value stays 0. Earned value and cost still count.
epic.noCurve: No plan curve: the planned window holds no working day, so planned value has nothing to be spread over. Earned value and cost still count.

dataQuality.title: Data quality
dataQuality.description: Where the data behind the other reports is missing or inconsistent. Each card names one finding, says what it means and lists the first cases. A finding is not a verdict on people: it marks a place where a number elsewhere deserves less trust.

summary.title: Overview
summary.tilesLabel: Headline counts, each linking to its card
summary.coverageNone: No done task in this period
summary.lateHint: of {{count}} worklogs with a known logging time
summary.sprintFigures: sprint figures moved since the freeze
summary.boardsHintResidual: boards without a team · unattributed done tasks: {{count}}

dataQuality.more: and {{count}} more (the list shows the first {{shown}})

scope.notTeam: This is a property of the connection, so the team filter does not narrow it.
scope.noTeam: This belongs to no team, so a single team's view lists none. Choose All teams or Unassigned to see it.
scope.boardList: Only the list of boards is not narrowed by the team; the done-task counts and the residual below follow the filter.

dataQuality.noSprintPerPerson: Sprint findings belong to a team's sprints, so they are not read for a single person.
dataQuality.notConfigured: No connection in scope has a work-category field configured, so this finding is not measured.

stat.unattributed: Done in a team-less sprint of no listed board

coverage.title: Done tasks without worklogs
coverage.explain: Done tasks that have no time logged at all. Without a worklog their actual effort is unknown, so the estimation reports cannot compare it with the estimate.

hours.title: Logged hours per member and working day
hours.explain: Hours that team members logged, divided by the working days they were on a roster. Read it against the configured length of a man-day: a figure far below it suggests that time is not being logged in full.

late.title: Late logging
late.explain: How long after the work started it was logged. Time logged days later is written from memory, which makes actual effort less reliable.

authors.title: Authors without a team
authors.explain: People who logged time while they were in no team. Their time is credited to no team's actual cost.

noEstimate.title: Tasks without an estimate
noEstimate.explain: Tasks with no estimate at all. They add no planned value and cannot be judged for accuracy.

noEpic.title: Tasks without an epic
noEpic.explain: Tasks that belong to no epic, so epic progress and epic-level planning never see them.

noWorkCategory.title: Tasks without a work category
noWorkCategory.explain: Tasks with no work category of their own or from their epic. They fall into “uncategorized” in every category breakdown.

unassigned.title: Done tasks without an assignee
unassigned.explain: Tasks that had no assignee when they were finished, so no person is credited with the work.

epicsNoEstimate.title: Epics without an estimate of their own
epicsNoEstimate.explain: Their budget is the sum of their children's estimates, so it changes whenever a child is added or re-estimated.

epicsNoDates.title: Epics without dates
epicsNoDates.explain: Epics missing a start or a due date. Without both, no plan curve (planned value over time) can be drawn.

epicsHorizon.title: Epics with dates far from today
epicsHorizon.explain: Both dates are set, but at least one lies more than ten years from the last derive, most likely a typo. These epics get no plan curve.

epicDrift.title: Epics that disagree with their children
epicDrift.explain: An epic that has not started while its children are active, is still open after every child is done, or is done while children are open.

outsideSprint.title: Work done outside any sprint
outsideSprint.explain: Tasks finished with no sprint (a Kanban flow, say). They count as delivered work but never in any sprint's velocity.

crossDomain.title: Tasks in another domain than their epic
crossDomain.explain: Done tasks whose epic belongs to a different domain. Which domain they count in depends on the domain view: delivered in (the task's own) or earned in (the epic's).

snapshotDrift.title: Sprint figures that moved since the freeze
snapshotDrift.explain: A closed sprint's figures are frozen when it closes. These live figures differ from the frozen ones, typically after a configuration change and a re-derive. Reports show the frozen figures and flag the sprint.

domainsNoOwner.title: Domains without an owner team
domainsNoOwner.explain: Their epics and backlog land in “No owner team”. An administrator can fix this in the metrics configuration.

unmappedStatuses.title: Statuses without a stage
unmappedStatuses.explain: Time spent in these Jira statuses counts as neither started nor done. An administrator maps them to a stage in the metrics configuration (Statuses).

unmappedBoards.title: Boards without a team
unmappedBoards.explain: Their sprints have no team and no frozen figures, and their tasks fall back to the assignee's team. An administrator maps a team to each board in the metrics configuration (Boards).

deriveWarnings.title: Derive warnings
deriveWarnings.explain: The latest successful derive of these connections skipped a step, so the reports that depend on it are missing or stale. An administrator can fix the cause in the metrics configuration.

baseline.reconstructedNote: Reconstructed: the snapshot was written by a derive that ran after the sprint closed, so it is a baseline rebuilt from history, not a true freeze.

warning.sprintFieldUnresolved: The sprint field could not be resolved, so the sprint step was skipped

late.distributionCaption: Every worklog of the period with a known logging time.
late.worstCaption: Up to 50 worklogs, the ones logged latest first.
late.noneMeasurable: No worklog in this period has a known logging time, so lateness cannot be measured.

dataQuality.hoursNone: No team member was on a roster in this period, so there is no figure per member-day.

groups.caption: Estimate and epic counts add the done and the open tasks. An epic can appear in several epic findings, so that column counts findings, not epics. A read narrowed to one connection lists only the teams that have a finding in it, so a silent team of another connection is left out.

dataQuality.unattributedNote_one: {{count}} done task was finished in a team-less sprint that belongs to none of the boards above (the sprint has no board, or its board is mapped but the sprint carries no team).
dataQuality.unattributedNote_other: {{count}} done tasks were finished in a team-less sprint that belongs to none of the boards above (the sprint has no board, or its board is mapped but the sprint carries no team).
dataQuality.coverageNone: No done task in this period, so there is no coverage to measure.

costMatrix.title: Cost matrix
costMatrix.description: The man-days people logged in the period, by the team the author belonged to on the day (rows) and by domain (columns), with the share of foreign work beside every row. Open a team to see its authors, an author to see one person.

levelTitle.UNIT: Man-days by author team and domain

caption.UNIT: Man-days logged in the period: author teams in rows, domains in columns, then the row total and the foreign work
caption.TEAM: Man-days logged in the period: the team's authors in rows, domains in columns, then the row total and the foreign work
caption.USER: Man-days logged in the period by this author: domains in columns, then the total and the foreign work

domainView.EPIC: Columns show the epic's domain — a task with no epic counts in its own domain.
domainView.TASK: Columns show the task's own domain, even when its epic belongs to another.

costMatrix.shareHint: Foreign man-days as a share of everything logged in the period.
costMatrix.foreignHint: Foreign work is time logged on tasks outside the author's own team's work: tasks of another team's sprint, or, when a task has no sprint team, tasks assigned to someone in another team. Time logged on an epic is foreign when the epic's domain belongs to another team. An unknown team is never counted as foreign.
costMatrix.foreignNone: Nothing was logged, so there is no share.

sprintNote.UNIT: The period follows sprints. Each team row reads the whole unit's sprint window (every team's sprints together); opening a team reads only that team's own sprints, so its figures can differ from its row here.
sprintNote.TEAM: The period follows sprints: this team's own sprints.

costMatrix.rounding: Every figure is its own exact sum, rounded once to two decimals. A total can therefore differ from the sum of the figures shown above it by up to 0.005 for each of them.

legend.label: Colour scale
legend.text: A more intense cell holds more man-days, up to {{max}} MD in one cell. The number in the cell is the figure; the shade only helps to find it.
